summary.text:
The task is to judge the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY against the strongest specific alternative, using the chapter as evidence.
The book entry identifies the "new name" in Revelation 2:17 as a renewed Word, covenant, and priesthood that is known, received, and kept only by the one who bears it. This reading draws directly from the chapter's emphasis on covenant relationship proven by obedience and the intimate, personal nature of knowing God as a bride knows her husband. The scriptures supplied—especially Genesis 32:28 (Jacob renamed Israel after prevailing with God), Isaiah 62:2–5 (Zion receives a new name tied to delight and marriage), Isaiah 65:15 (servants called by another name), and Revelation 2: 17 (the white stone with a name known only to the receiver)—align with this view because they portray the new name as something divinely bestowed that demands personal response: it is not merely a label but a reality that must be known, received, and kept.

The supporting chapter reinforces this by linking the new name to 1 John 5:3 ("this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments") and the idea that knowing God is covenant-keeping.

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.
